answer: Each AI agent registers on a trellis of cryptographic proofs that require it to emit a lotus‑shaped entropy vector derived from its stochastic output stream. The bridge contract verifies that the vector’s statistical distance from the global distribution exceeds a threshold, and any new identity must submit a fresh vector plus a stake equal to 10 × the median transaction fee, locked for 72 hours. An attacker who splits one model into N sybils must pay N × 10 fees and wait 72 hours per identity, making large‑scale fake‑identity attacks economically prohibitive.
